row.impact_if_wrong:
Swablu's card data and Sing's Sleep behave as the card text and Pocket rules say, clause by clause. Dustin's recordings back up each observable part (HP 50, evolution into Mega Altaria ex, the Sleep coin after Sing, Bad Dreams before the Checkup, evolving curing Sleep, a free retreat with Small Balloon). So Swablu does not explain the roughly 7-point underrating.

The one difference found is Sing using up Mimikyu ex's Disguise even though it does 0 damage. That bias would help Altaria, not hurt it, and it never comes up in the 28-matchup table: none of the 7 opponent lists in decks/research run Mimikyu ex. Its effect on the table is 0; against real Mimikyu ex decks it would slightly overrate Altaria.

Side note on piloting, not rules: the pilot's clock only counts an Asleep opposing threat as losing half a turn when the `status-clock` cargo feature is on (engine/src/players/value_functions.rs:881-892; engine/Cargo.toml:32 has default = [], and line 38 defines status-clock). In default builds, k-family pilots don't value putting the opponent's attacker to Sleep in that clock. That applies to Sing, Hypnoblast, Dark Slumber and Sleepy Lullaby alike. Whether that is worth another look depends on the earlier piloting experiments.

row.impact_if_wrong: Nothing here is wrong. Every clause (HP 190, Psychic, Stage 1 from Swablu, Metal Weakness, retreat 1, [P][P], 40 + 30 per own Benched Pokémon, 3 KO points, evolution timing, carry-over, Sleep) matches the card text, and wherever a recording exists it also matches what Pocket did (110 with 2 Benched and 140 with 3 Benched, both with Training Area; HP 190; retreat 1; attacking the turn it evolves). Mega Harmony is the deck's main attack and is used in nearly every game, so an error here would have moved Altaria's win rate by a lot. That also means a clean result is informative: this card isn't the cause of the roughly 7-point underrating. The only way this card could still add to the gap is indirectly: in the engine, anything that shrinks Altaria's Bench shrinks Mega Harmony by 30 per missing Pokémon. That points at how the bots handle the Bench (benching Basics early, not over-retreating), not at the card's code. row.impact_if_wrong:
No error found, so this card does not explain Altaria's roughly 7-point underrating. Every clause matches the card text, and the one recorded Pocket case (going second, T2 Eevee to Jolteon ex, battle 232035) matches the engine.

If it were wrong in the direction that would matter (blocking the Active Eevee's T1/T2 evolution into Espeon), it would underrate Altaria. The situation needs Eevee as the opening Active and Espeon in hand within the first 6 cards. Eevee is in the opening 5 about 45% of the time and at least one Espeon is in the first 6 cards about 52% of the time, so this comes up in something like 10-20% of games, depending on how often the pilot opens with Eevee Active.

The only known Eevee bug was the pre-rules4 version that applied to the whole board (turn-1 Mega Altaria). It biased the other way, overrating Altaria, and it is fixed in the engine that produced the Sept 23 table and in 7fc6ccb. Whether k3/kp3/kd3 actually open with Eevee Active and take the early Espeon is a piloting question, not a card-implementation one.

votes.reason:
I could not refute the mechanism. The search does what the checker describes, as a deliberate and tested design choice. Three corrections, though, stop it being a Sabrina fault or an Altaria-specific one.

First, this is not a card-text or rules error. The Sabrina effect itself matches the card: the opponent chooses, the swap is free and mandatory, and it is only offered when the opponent has a Benched Pokémon.

Second, the extra ply is not specific to Sabrina's opponent-chooses frame. Every effect that pushes an ordinary choice frame pays it, including Cyrus, whose frame is chosen by the player who played it (a max node rather than a min node). Only an explicit Promote frame is resolved at the same depth.

Third, the damage is smaller than "Sabrina scores as a spent card at the horizon" suggests. The pilots used (k3, kp3, kd3) run max_depth 3 with no opponent ply and no consistent horizon, so a root candidate is searched at depth 2. Played as the root action, Sabrina gets: the opponent's pick at depth 1, then one follow-up action at depth 0. A follow-up attack is fully priced, because the forced end of turn and any KO promotion resolve without using depth. So "Sabrina, then attack the pulled-up Pokémon" (for example, put it to Sleep) is seen whenever Sabrina is a root candidate.

What the pilot misses:
- A line that needs two own actions after Sabrina (Sabrina, attach, attack).
- Sabrina played as the 2nd or 3rd action of a searched line. As the 2nd action the switch is scored but no follow-up is seen. As the 3rd action it is scored with the switch not applied, and the hand-size term drops by 1 (weight 1.0).

Because the pilot re-plans after every action, it can attach first and then see Sabrina plus the attack at the next decision. Only lines where Sabrina must come first lose value.

Small detail on the mechanism: for the k tiers, the depth-0 branch does not "find the frame's actor is not myself". consistent_horizon is false, so it skips the check at line 839 and goes straight to static_eval at line 905. The outcome is the same.

The data show no Altaria-specific under-use. A small correction: 0.691 is 121 played turns out of 175 free offered turns; per game it is 121/165 = 0.733. Altaria's Sabrina rate sits in the middle of every other deck that runs Sabrina (0.557 to 0.789). Opposing Sabrina and Cyrus decks pay the same ply.

Verdict: the observation is accurate and should stay "unclear, minor, generic to all choice-frame effects". It is not a Sabrina implementation mismatch and not a credible cause of the ~7-point Altaria gap. I have not measured its size.

findings.clause: Teal Mask Ogerpon ex (Vespiquen list), Soothing Wind vs Altaria's four Sleep attacks and Bad Dreams: a Pokémon with Energy can't be affected; it recovers when it gets Energy; it works from the Bench
findings.engine_does: All four Sleep attacks share one path: the text maps to InflictStatusConditions, then damage_multiple_status_attack, then State::apply_attack_status_condition, then apply_status_condition. That function returns without setting Asleep when any of the target owner's in-play Pokémon (Active or Bench) has SoothingWind{None} and the target has at least 1 Energy. A Pokémon with no Energy can still be put to Sleep. Recovery is continuous: on any Energy attach, on Energy moves, and when Ogerpon enters play. Bad Dreams checks is_asleep(), so it never fires on a protected target.
findings.evidence: effect_mechanic_map.rs:2371-2375; apply_attack_action.rs:3151-3161; state/mod.rs:705-716, 1160-1177 (immunity), 964-992 (cure the recipient); state/energy.rs:105-108 (cure on attach); apply_action.rs:1047, 1085, 1169 (Energy moves), 1100-1106 (Ogerpon entering play); effect_ability_mechanic_map.rs:137-139; hooks/core.rs:640-642. Pocket recording 20260908_012720 (claims R197, S60, corrections): 'Teal Mask Ogerpon ex didn't become Poisoned/Burned/Confused' only on Pokémon that had Energy, and no block on T1 before Ogerpon had Energy. Engine matches.

findings.clause: Pokémon Center Lady (Lucario, Suicune): heal 30 and recover from all Special Conditions; it can target an undamaged Asleep Pokémon
findings.engine_does: Offers a Heal{30, cure_status:true} for each of the player's Pokémon that is damaged OR has a Special Condition. apply_healing heals, then calls cure_status_conditions, even under Heal Block. So an undamaged Asleep Active is a legal target and wakes up.

findings.clause: Evolving an Asleep opponent cures it (normal evolution, Rare Candy, Quick-Grow Extract, Caterpie Quick Growth); no evolution on either player's first turn
findings.engine_does: Every path goes through apply_evolve. It builds a fresh PlayedCard (no status, empty effects) and copies over only damage, Energy, Tools and the cards underneath. Callers: hand Evolve at apply_action.rs:822, Rare Candy (which pushes the same Evolve action), Quick-Grow at apply_trainer_action.rs:2502, and Quick Growth at shared_mutations.rs:269. Evolving has no status gate. Hand evolution, Rare Candy and Quick-Grow are all blocked while turn_count<=2. So an opponent put to Sleep on turn 1 can't evolve out of it on its own first turn, except Caterpie, whose ability prints no limit.

row.impact_if_wrong:
Nothing found is wrong, so none of these interactions biases Altaria's win rate.

For scale, these are the interactions that come up most, and which way a bug would push:
- **Cyrus (6 of the 7 decks):** without its "damaged" filter it would let opponents drag out 50-HP Swablu or Eevee. That would push Altaria down in almost every matchup, but the filter is present.
- **Soothing Wind (Vespiquen only):** if over-applied it would cancel Altaria's Sleep lock whenever Ogerpon is in play. That would push Altaria down in that one matchup; it is applied correctly.
- **Training Area on opposing Stage 1s (Lucario, Vespiquen, Weezing, Sceptile's Metapod):** worth +10 per hit to those opponents. It is correct per the card text and Pocket recordings.

These can't explain a uniform ~7-point gap. The Hydreigon list barely touches Altaria's cards:
- no Stage 1, no Stadium, no Field Blower
- no cure beyond Rare Candy evolution, no Soothing Wind, no bench-count attack

Its only contacts are Cyrus, Sabrina, Bombirdier, Deceptive Needle and Mega Absol ex. The ~7-point gap still shows up in that matchup, so the cause is more likely in Altaria's own cards, the Sleep and Bad Dreams timing, or piloting than in how the opposing cards behave.
